title: The Choir of Ironhollow
premise: Xanthe Brightwater, a debt-bound scribe in the guild of Ironhollow, has spent years recording trades in impossible things while keeping their own name off every ledger. When a dying courier presses them a map to the king's true heart—a caged soul held beneath the palace—Xanthe learns the crown itself is a devouring thing that feeds on borrowed lives, including the debt that binds Xanthe. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and drawn to Serah, the knight sworn to protect the false king, Xanthe must choose between erasing themselves from history or writing themselves into a rebellion. In the end, Xanthe burns the guild's ledgers to unbind every debtor, shatters the crown with the map's forgotten ritual, and—having lost their invisibility forever—chooses to stay beside Serah and help rebuild a kingdom that finally knows their name.
about_author: Zephyrine Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a cluttered study full of unlabeled keys, insisting that every locked door deserves at least one story.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Names
chapters.summary: In Xanthe's POV, we see the guild of Ironhollow through its ledgers: trades in memories, shadows, and years, all recorded in Xanthe's careful hand while their own debts keep them bound and invisible. A dying courier collapses into the scriptorium, pressing a bloodstained map into Xanthe's hands and whispering that the king is already gone. The emotional beat is reluctant awakening—the terror of being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Crown Devours
chapters.summary: Fleeing the guild's enforcers, Xanthe deciphers the map with help from Serah, a knight whose duty to guard the hollow-eyed king wars with her growing suspicion that he wears a stolen face. Alternating between Xanthe's and Serah's POVs, they uncover the crown's nature: it eats souls to sustain its wearer, and Xanthe's own debt-mark is a leash leading back to it. The beat is deepening intimacy and dread as love kindles against duty.

chapters.title: The Ledger Must Burn
chapters.summary: Captured by the guild and brought before its Master, who is revealed to be the crown's first victim and willing servant, Xanthe is offered freedom in exchange for the map. In a climactic choice, Xanthe instead sets fire to the master ledger, unbinding every debtor—including themselves—as chaos erupts. Serah turns her blade against her oath to buy Xanthe time. The beat is defiant sacrifice; identity claimed at last, whatever the cost.

chapters.title: A Kingdom That Knows My Name
chapters.summary: Beneath the palace, following the map's final path, Xanthe performs the forgotten rite to release the king's caged soul while the crown-thing fights back with memories of everyone Xanthe erased. Serah anchors them with her voice and her hand, and together they shatter the crown, freeing the true king—diminished but alive. The resolution offers justice outside any law: no trial, only truth spoken aloud. Xanthe, visible and unbound, chooses to stay. The beat is hard-won belonging.
